title: One setup, twelve repos
scenario:
A platform team keeps a good Claude Code setup in one repo: two skills, a format hook and a GitHub MCP server. Eleven other repos want it. The team also looks at a plugin from a third-party marketplace. You review their plan.

Use the exhibit. The team, the plugin and the notes are made up for this case. File names and scopes are from the vendors' pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
PLAN (made up)

  1. Copy .claude/skills/, the hook and .mcp.json into each
     of the 11 repos by hand.
  2. Install "quick-lint" from the third-party marketplace
     "acme-tools". Its listing says: 2 skills, 1 hook,
     1 MCP server. Nobody has opened its files.
  3. Ana installed the team plugin at user scope. Ben, in
     the same repo, does not have it.
  4. Developers have 30 plugins enabled. Most are never used.
     Sessions feel crowded.

questions.prompt: Plan item 1: what does Anthropic suggest instead of copying by hand?

options.text: Package the skills, hook and MCP server as one plugin
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says to package a setup as a plugin when a second repository needs it. A plugin installs as one unit.

options.text: Put the whole setup into one very long CLAUDE.md file
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is instructions Claude reads every session, not a package. For a setup a second repo needs, Anthropic points to a plugin.

options.text: Turn the whole setup into one subagent that copies it
options.explanation: A subagent is a worker with its own context, not a way to share a setup between repos.

options.text: Copy only the skills, since hooks can't be shared at all
options.explanation: Hooks can be shared. A plugin can hold hooks next to skills and MCP servers.

questions.prompt: Plan item 2: a teammate says "it comes from a marketplace, so it is safe". What is true?

options.text: Marketplace plugins run in a sandbox, so their hooks can't harm
options.explanation: Anthropic says plugin hooks and MCP servers run outside the sandbox, with your user privileges.

options.text: A marketplace reviews every plugin before it lists it there
options.explanation: Anthropic calls a marketplace a catalog, not a hosted store. Its name says who publishes the catalog, not what a plugin does.

options.text: Permission rules check every command the plugin runs itself
options.explanation: Anthropic says permission rules cover the tool calls Claude makes, not the code a plugin runs by itself.

options.text: The name says who runs the catalog; read the hook before install
options.explanation: Right. A plugin can run code with your user privileges, and a marketplace name is not a review. Read its hooks and servers first.

questions.prompt: Plan item 3: how should the team plugin reach everyone in this repo?

options.text: Install at local scope, which shares it with the whole team
options.explanation: Local scope is for you in this repository only.

options.text: Use project scope; each person still installs it on their machine
options.explanation: Right. Project scope enables it for everyone through the committed .claude/settings.json, but each collaborator still installs it.

options.text: Keep user scope, which turns it on for every user of the repo
options.explanation: User scope is for you, in every project on your own computer. It does not reach Ben.

options.text: Rename the plugin so the marketplace pushes it to all users
options.explanation: No scope works by renaming. Project scope is the one for a whole repository.

questions.prompt: Plan item 4: why do 30 enabled plugins crowd sessions that don't use them?

options.text: Plugins only load when used, so the cause must be something else
options.explanation: Anthropic says an enabled plugin is part of every session, not only the sessions where you use it.

options.text: Each enabled plugin adds its skill names and descriptions every turn
options.explanation: Right. Names and descriptions sit in context on every turn, and its MCP servers run. Disable the plugins you don't use.

options.text: Each enabled plugin loads the full text of every skill at start
options.explanation: Only names and descriptions are there every turn. The full text of a skill loads when it is used.

options.text: Plugins slow sessions only on the first day after an install
options.explanation: The cost is not a one-day thing. An enabled plugin is part of every session.
